justification: Standard: adds page ranges to Waverley's config and one page-based rule to the tagger that decides which development types a rule shows for. Not Minor: it changes tagging for 38 live rows once applied. Not Critical: the dry run narrows 0 served rows (the only direction that hides a control), nothing is written by this change, and the apply is a separate step that asks first and keeps a backup table.

pre_impl.existing_data: 38 served Waverley rows read no_config (DQ-33 = 38): pages 11 (contents), 181 (Annexure B8-1), 187 (general notes), 193 (Part C1), 417-418 (Annexure E1-1), 419-425 (Annexure E2-1). Their headings are numbers like 7.9 or (ix) that name no Part the config knows. Pages read from the live R2 file waverley-dcp-2022.pdf v1.2 on 2026-11-24.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The other chat's prompt said 498 rows and a Part that must be set first. 460 of those were fixed on 2026-11-23 by the plan's page map; the 38 left sit on pages that map names no Part for.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: northern_beaches and cumberland already use part_pages for rows with no Part. Waverley now does the same, with ranges written only where the page itself names its Part. reference_pages is new: pages that hold no control read config_all like annexure headings already do.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A page in no list stays no_config and is never guessed; a row with its own valid Part keeps it.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A rule from a contents or general-notes page, or an annexure, is hidden from or shown to the wrong development type.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A reference page row falls to no_config, an annexure row finds no Part from its page, a page in no list is guessed, or the plan narrows a served row.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Two deliberate breaks (reference pages ignored, no part ranges) each failed 2 of 8 tests.
falsifiable_check.observed_green: 8 new tests and 12 related tests pass; 294 applicability, waverley and tagger tests pass. The Waverley retag dry run changes 2 values, narrows 0 served rows, and leaves 0 served dev-type no_config.

functions.name: _on_reference_page
functions.input: a document id and a PDF page number
functions.output: true only when the council's config lists that page as holding no control
functions.if_none: no document id or no page is never a reference page

functions.name: tag_with_provenance
functions.input: a rule's text, document id, Part and PDF page
functions.output: zones, development types and where each came from

values.if_missing: the file is read at import, so a missing file stops the import rather than silently tagging nothing

queries.purpose: No new query; the retag script reads the same current rows of the named council as before and writes only after the owners go with a backup table
queries.where_clause: unchanged: current rows of the named councils, writes only after the owner's go with a backup table

break_it.scenario: A rule on a general-notes page really is about one development type.
break_it.what_happens: It would read config_all and show for every type.
break_it.how: Only pages 11 and 187 are listed, each with the sentence that shows it is a contents list or general notes; showing a rule too widely is noise, hiding it is the harm.

break_it.scenario: A page range is wrong by a page.
break_it.what_happens: A row would take a neighbouring Part.
break_it.how: Each range cites the page that opens it and the page that opens the next; the test checks ranges do not overlap and each cites a page.

break_it.scenario: A row already carries its own valid Part.
break_it.what_happens: The page range could overwrite it.
break_it.how: The range is used only when the row's own Part is not a valid code.

break_it.scenario: A row sits on a page in no list.
break_it.what_happens: It could be given a guessed Part.
break_it.how: It stays no_config and is counted by DQ-33.

break_it.scenario: The retag script reads the same current rows and rewrites provenance for all 11,350 Waverley rows, not only the changed ones.
break_it.what_happens: A mistake in the plan would touch every Waverley row.
break_it.how: The dry run prints values changed (2), served rows narrowed (0) and predicted sources first; the apply makes a full backup table and aborts if the row count differs.

post_merge.manual_verify: python scripts/retag_applicability_slug_docids.py --councils waverley (dry run), then --apply after the owner's go with the printed counts; then python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-33 reads 0 and python scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py OC-17 exits 0.
